concerns: No direct experimental evidence in the canonical set that reversible affinity capture + mild elution preserves membrane-protected cargo or that such a workflow recovers spike-in tracers as membrane-protected — this is the core untested assumption.
Risk of selective loss or enrichment of EV subpopulations or enrichment of non-vesicular complexes that bind the capture reagent is plausible and not experimentally excluded by the cited evidence.

Elution chemistries could disrupt membranes and invalidate the proposed detergent/protease protection readout; MISEV recommends orthogonal controls but does not validate any specific reversible-capture chemistry.
Manufacturability claims (cassette-compatible, low-shear, scalable) are unproven for the proposed capture media in the canonical evidence; availability and vendor formats are unverified.
Proposal relies on qualitative gates without numeric acceptance criteria; that increases subjectivity and could impede comparability and regulatory clarity unless quantitative follow-up is performed.

Translational risk: NHP intranasal biodistribution data (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution) show negligible brain uptake after intranasal administration, highlighting that analytic identity of a bounded fraction is necessary but insufficient to establish in vivo exposure across species.
conclusion: Not supported as written. The proposal aligns with MISEV2023 recommendations for orthogonal, membrane-protection–based EV identification and reasonably acknowledges translational biodistribution uncertainty, but the canonical evidence set does not provide direct experimental support that a reversible, low-shear affinity-capture pre-enrichment preserves intact EV membrane protection or reproducibly improves pilot-scale recovery versus the stated comparators. Key methodological and manufacturing claims remain unproven by the supplied evidence.
evidence_gap: No supplied canonical evidence demonstrates that a reversible, low-shear affinity-capture operation (with mild elution) preserves membrane integrity/protection and recovers an exogenous intact-EV spike-in while giving qualitatively improved particle/mass yield at pilot/manufacturing-relevant scale. There is also no direct evidence here that the proposed capture/elution chemistries and formats exist or are compatible with closed, cassette-style sterile workflows, nor data showing assay compatibility of the proposed capture reagents with the protection assays. Finally, there is no canonical evidence linking an analytically defined bounded fraction produced by this specific reversible-capture->SEC workflow to improved in vivo exposure or translational biodistribution (the NHP data instead raise concerns about intranasal recoverability).
